sessionTitle: Powering the next AI frontier with a unified data platform

announcements.name: SharePoint and OneDrive shortcuts GA in OneLake
announcements.shortDescription: These join recently announced SAP and Oracle support, extending zero-ETL data access.
announcements.longDescription: SharePoint and OneDrive shortcuts are now generally available in OneLake, joining the recently announced general availability of SAP and Oracle support. These shortcuts extend OneLake's ability to create a single pane of glass across all data with zero ETL, zero effort, and zero cost, regardless of where the data resides—on-premises, in any cloud, in databases, apps, or files.

announcements.name: New OneLake source previews
announcements.shortDescription: Public preview for Dremio and Azure Database for MySQL, with Azure Monitor and AWS Glue coming soon to bring observability data alongside business data.
announcements.longDescription: OneLake adds public preview support for Dremio and Azure Database for MySQL, with Azure Monitor and AWS Glue coming soon. These new sources allow the whole observability data estate to be brought into OneLake to join with the business data estate, continuing the effort to add more data sources with zero ETL.

announcements.name: GPU query acceleration for Fabric Data Warehouse (limited preview)
announcements.shortDescription: Demonstrated up to 8x faster single queries and over 100x at 64 concurrent queries, enabled via a one-click workspace setting.
announcements.longDescription: Microsoft announced the limited preview of query acceleration in the Fabric Data Warehouse through GPUs, enabled with a simple one-click setup. On TPC-H benchmarks the GPU-accelerated warehouse delivered an average 8X performance improvement over the CPU-powered Fabric Data Warehouse for single queries, and acceleration improved to roughly 25 times faster when running 16 concurrent queries. A demo later showed roughly 89% of queries were accelerated for a given warehouse.

announcements.name: Agent skills for Fabric expanded
announcements.shortDescription: Beyond analytical engines, agents can now generate Power BI reports and provision full medallion architectures from a prompt.
announcements.longDescription: Microsoft announced an expansion of agent skills for Fabric, which give agents the expertise to work with Fabric correctly and with best practices. Released about three months ago for working with the analytical engines, the skill set now expands so agents can also create Power BI reports. A demo showed using Fabric's agent skills repo with GitHub Copilot in the CLI to provision an entire medallion architecture and customer data pipeline—including a LakeHouse artifact and notebook—from a single prompt.

announcements.name: Custom live pools
announcements.shortDescription: Reduces Spark pool startup from 3–5 minutes to 3–5 seconds via pre-warming.
announcements.longDescription: Custom live pools reduce the long Spark pool startup times customers used to experience when loading libraries and network security settings, from 3 to 5 minutes down to anywhere between 3 to 5 seconds. Users can schedule pools to be pre-warmed with all their configurations at a set time each morning, avoiding long startup waits when attaching compute to notebooks. The demo also referenced the up-to-date runtime including Spark 4.0 and Delta 4.0.

announcements.name: Fabric ontology integrations
announcements.shortDescription: New connections across Foundry, Copilot Studio, and Agent 365 [inferred], still in preview ahead of GA later this year.
announcements.longDescription: Building on the Fabric ontology announced a few months ago, Microsoft announced new integrations across Foundry, Copilot Studio, and Agent 365, expanding support for ontologies. Ontologies extend semantics beyond reporting analytics to explain to AI how the business works, including business processes, real-time feeds, policies, and actions, so the AI can participate in business processes. The capability is still in preview and becoming more capable as it moves toward GA coming later this year.

announcements.name: Planning in Fabric now GA
announcements.shortDescription: An end-to-end enterprise planning workload for budgets, forecasts, and scenarios, rolling out to remaining regions over the coming weeks.
announcements.longDescription: Planning in Fabric, a workload announced about three months ago in preview, is now generally available and will roll out to the rest of the regions over the next couple of weeks. It is an end-to-end enterprise planning tool that allows teams to manage budgets, forecasts, scenarios, and targets, serving as the source of truth for what should happen in the future. It is fully integrated with Fabric across the experience, security model, and OneLake configuration, with write-back to Fabric SQL databases.

announcements.name: Apps in Fabric (preview)
announcements.shortDescription: Production-grade line-of-business apps on governed data, built on the Rayfin SDK [inferred], a type-safe, decorator-based optimizer for agentic development.
announcements.longDescription: Microsoft introduced Apps in Fabric in preview for the first time, allowing creation of production-grade line-of-business applications running on top of governed data. It provides one managed backend covering functions, storage, security, and authentication, designed to be secure from the ground up and serving as a great environment for vibe-coded applications. It is built on the Rayfin SDK [inferred], a type-safe, decorator-based code optimizer for agentic development, with project setup driven by a single command from the Rayfin CLI.

announcements.name: Agent-driven BI apps
announcements.shortDescription: Custom web dashboards built against semantic models using the same Rayfin SDK.
announcements.longDescription: Extending the Rayfin-based applications, Microsoft showed agent-driven BI apps that let users build custom web pages and dashboards tracking data based on semantic models. Using the same Rayfin SDK, users can add custom data apps directly in Fabric, where Copilot in VS Code scaffolds the project, wires up auth, and connects to governed Fabric assets. The agent can reach for a Power BI capability to generate interactive visuals directly against semantic models without rebuilding the foundation maintained by the analytics team.

announcements.name: Operations agents now GA
announcements.shortDescription: Autonomous virtual team members that monitor signals and act in the background, with new chat-based authoring, root cause analysis, and Microsoft Teams integration.
announcements.longDescription: Operations agents are now generally available. Unlike chatbots that answer questions, these are virtual team members that monitor signals and react autonomously in the background, constantly looking at what's going on and taking actions. They are configured entirely through natural language with no coding required, and new capabilities at GA include chat-based authoring, root cause analysis, and Microsoft Teams integration. A demo showed setting up an agent to monitor customer churn 24/7.
